# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Mia Ortiz
**Incident Date:** 11/13/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 100 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Scarlett Baker, CCC-SLP

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Mia was engaged in art activity at 100 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Mia exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 3 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Scarlett Baker, CCC-SLP implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Mia responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Mia participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Mia was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Charles Ortiz at 315.472.5678. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Scarlett Baker
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/26 at 100 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Martinez on 5/4/26

**Report filed by:** Scarlett Baker, CCC-SLP
**Filed:** 11/13/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Jackson participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Baldwinsville TEC. Session began at 9:00 AM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

Contacted Timothy Stewart at 315.432.5678 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Jackson has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Owen Reyes, PhD, BCBA
**Date signed:** 11/17/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**TRANSITION 1:** 95 Geiger ICF → Baldwinsville TEC
Time: 10:15 AM
Trigger: Unexpected staff change (regular driver unavailable)
Client Response: Moderate anxiety, verbal questioning, increased pacing

Henry demonstrated heightened anxiety when informed of transition from 
95 Geiger ICF to Baldwinsville TEC with unfamiliar driver. 
Environmental factors noted:
- Different vehicle than typical transport
- Substitute staff member instead of usual Henry Myers

**TRANSITION 2:** Baldwinsville TEC → Liverpool TEC
Time: 2:15 PM
Trigger: Schedule modification due to building maintenance
Client Response: Mild agitation, requesting return to familiar setting

**SCHEDULE DISRUPTION ANALYSIS:**
Originally scheduled appointment with Dr. Patterson at Baldwinsville TEC on 
April 17, 2026 was 
rescheduled to 4/29/26 
due to provider illness. Henry exhibited increased anxiety and repetitive questioning 
about appointment status.

**PARENT CONTACT:**
Diane Carter contacted at (315) 499-3456 to discuss 
schedule sensitivity. Parent reported Henry frequently references upcoming appointments 
at home and struggles with last-minute changes.

**SENSORY ENVIRONMENT ASSESSMENT:**
95 Geiger ICF: Familiar lighting, low noise level, preferred seating available
Baldwinsville TEC: Moderate noise level, fluorescent lighting, multiple peer interactions
Liverpool TEC: High activity level, variable noise, open floor plan

Consultation with Sebastian Lopez, Psy.D. scheduled for 05/27/2026 
to assess sensory processing needs and environmental accommodation recommendations.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Increase transition warnings from 5 minutes to 15 minutes advance notice
- Environmental modifications at Baldwinsville TEC:
  * Provide noise-canceling headphones during high-activity periods
  * Designate quiet space for breaks
- Schedule consistency protocol - avoid changes within 48 hours when possible
- Provider coordination for appointment preparation with visual schedule

**FOLLOW-UP:**
Meeting with Diane Carter scheduled 
5/5/26 
to review environmental sensitivities.

Contact Sebastian Lopez, Psy.D. at 315-461-5678 for sensory consultation.

**Documented by:** Henry Myers
**Date:** 10/27/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

## SKILL ACQUISITION SESSION

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Wyatt participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Cicero TEC. Session began at 2:00 PM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 77% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 90% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 86% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 79%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**
Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
Wyatt demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
Wyatt practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Sophia Castillo, Ph.D. supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Carol Kelly at (315) 478-9012 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Wyatt has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Matthew Lopez
**Date signed:** 10/27/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

Victoria practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Aiden Martinez, Ph.D. supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

Contacted Angela Ortiz at 315.436.7890 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Victoria has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Alexander Lewis
**Date signed:** 10/06/2025

# UCP SESSION NOTE - ENVIRONMENTAL TRIGGER ANALYSIS

**Client:** Robinson, Amelia C.
**Session Date:** 11/06/2025
**Locations Observed:** 92 Geiger ICF, Baldwinsville TEC, Liverpool TEC
**Observing Staff:** Elizabeth Hill

---

## ENVIRONMENTAL TRIGGER DOCUMENTATION

**TRANSITION 1:** 92 Geiger ICF → Baldwinsville TEC
Time: 8:45 AM
Trigger: Unexpected staff change (regular driver unavailable)
Client Response: Moderate anxiety, verbal questioning, increased pacing

Amelia demonstrated heightened anxiety when informed of transition from 
92 Geiger ICF to Baldwinsville TEC with unfamiliar driver. 
Environmental factors noted:
- Different vehicle than typical transport
- Substitute staff member instead of usual Elizabeth Hill

**TRANSITION 2:** Baldwinsville TEC → Liverpool TEC
Time: 1:30 PM
Trigger: Schedule modification due to building maintenance
Client Response: Mild agitation, requesting return to familiar setting

**SCHEDULE DISRUPTION ANALYSIS:**
Originally scheduled appointment with Dr. Mitchell at Baldwinsville TEC on 
4/15/2026 was 
rescheduled to 04/30/2026 
due to provider illness. Amelia exhibited increased anxiety and repetitive questioning 
about appointment status.

**PARENT CONTACT:**
Sandra Robinson contacted at 315.444.9012 to discuss 
schedule sensitivity. Parent reported Amelia frequently references upcoming appointments 
at home and struggles with last-minute changes.

**SENSORY ENVIRONMENT ASSESSMENT:**
92 Geiger ICF: Familiar lighting, low noise level, preferred seating available
Baldwinsville TEC: Moderate noise level, fluorescent lighting, multiple peer interactions
Liverpool TEC: High activity level, variable noise, open floor plan

Consultation with Dr. Mitchell scheduled for 5/23/2026 
to assess sensory processing needs and environmental accommodation recommendations.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Increase transition warnings from 5 minutes to 15 minutes advance notice
- Environmental modifications at Baldwinsville TEC:
  * Provide noise-canceling headphones during high-activity periods
  * Designate quiet space for breaks
- Schedule consistency protocol - avoid changes within 48 hours when possible
- Provider coordination for appointment preparation with visual schedule

**FOLLOW-UP:**
Meeting with Sandra Robinson scheduled 
5/04/2026 
to review environmental sensitivities.

Contact Dr. Mitchell at 315-467-8901 for sensory consultation.

**Documented by:** Elizabeth Hill
**Date:** 11/06/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**Client:** Ross, Zoey
**Incident Date:** 10/21/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 92 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Elijah Lewis, M.Ed.

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Zoey was engaged in art activity at 92 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Zoey exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 5 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Elijah Lewis, M.Ed. implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Zoey responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Zoey participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Zoey was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Samuel Ross at 315-443-9012. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Elijah Lewis
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 92 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Foster on 04/29/2026

**Report filed by:** Elijah Lewis, M.Ed.
**Filed:** 10/21/2025

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Ella participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Chadwicks TEC. Session began at 2:00 PM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 79% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 89% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 90% accuracy across 15 trials

Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end.

Ella practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Charlotte Murphy, M.A. supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Jason Cook at (315)517-7890 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Ella has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Alexander Diaz
**Date signed:** 11/24/2025

Activity: Cooperative board game

been initiating play with siblings at home more frequently. Contact maintained via daily communication log.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Continue social skills group at Syracuse TEC
- Increase peer interaction opportunities during unstructured time
- Collaborate with Sophia Garcia, RN for social-emotional assessment

**Documentation:** Luke Castillo

1. Therapeutic processing of incident
2. Safety planning reinforcement
3. Skill rebuilding for emotion regulation

Chloe participated in cognitive-behavioral processing with Evelyn Garcia.

Discussion topics:
- Event sequence understanding using visual timeline
- Emotional identification (anger, frustration, feeling out of control)
- Alternative response strategies (asking for break, using calm-down space)
- Safety understanding (why restraint was necessary)

recognized inappropriate choice and impact on others.

Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Chloe.

- Home-program consistency for emotion regulation strategies

- De-escalation support at home (offering break space, reducing demands)
- Communication protocols between home and program

- Modified reinforcement schedule

- Dosage adjustment made
- Continue current regimen with modifications

Focus areas identified:

Parent reported Matthew has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Jacob Howard
**Date signed:** 10/23/2025

# UCP POST-CRISIS RECOVERY SESSION NOTE

**Client:** Aria P. Ruiz
**Recovery Session Date:** 10/19/2025
**Original Incident Date:** 4/18/2026
**Location:** 88 Geiger ICF
**Staff:** Riley Richardson
**Clinical Supervisor:** Emma Cox, BSN

---

## POST-CRISIS THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION

**INCIDENT REFERENCE:**
Critical incident on 4/18/2026 at 88 Geiger ICF.
Incident Report ID: INC-2026-2509
Type: Physical aggression toward peer and staff, property destruction
Duration: Escalation 6 minutes, restraint 24 minutes

TIME SINCE INCIDENT: 48 hours

**CURRENT SESSION PURPOSE:**
1. Therapeutic processing of incident
2. Safety planning reinforcement
3. Skill rebuilding for emotion regulation
4. Relationship repair with staff and peers

**SESSION ACTIVITIES:**

**THERAPEUTIC PROCESSING:**
Aria participated in cognitive-behavioral processing with Riley Richardson.

Discussion topics:
- Event sequence understanding using visual timeline
- Emotional identification (anger, frustration, feeling out of control)
- Alternative response strategies (asking for break, using calm-down space)
- Safety understanding (why restraint was necessary)

Aria's insight: Demonstrated good understanding of event sequence, identified trigger, 
recognized inappropriate choice and impact on others.

**SAFETY PLANNING:**
Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Aria.

**NEW SAFETY MEASURES IMPLEMENTED:**
Following incident on 4/18/2026:
1. Individual activity schedule - Implemented 4/19/2026
2. Enhanced visual supports for emotion regulation - Implemented 4/19/26
3. Enhanced monitoring during peer activities (1:2 ratio)

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Joint session with Jennifer Ruiz and Jacob Ruiz.

Parents contacted at (315) 445-7890 to confirm session attendance.

Discussion points:
- Home-program consistency for emotion regulation strategies
- Warning sign recognition (escalating voice volume, body tension, pacing)
- De-escalation support at home (offering break space, reducing demands)
- Communication protocols between home and program

**STAFF RELATIONSHIP REPAIR:**
Aria met individually with staff involved in incident.
Facilitated by: Emma Cox, BSN

Process included: Aria's verbal apology, staff reassurance of continued support, 
discussion of moving forward. Staff reported positive interaction quality.

**BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT PLAN UPDATES:**
Modified BSP implemented April 19, 2026 following comprehensive review.

Changes include:
- Enhanced antecedent strategies (increased warnings before transitions)
- Additional teaching of replacement behaviors (requesting break using visual card)
- Updated crisis protocols (specific de-escalation sequence)
- Modified reinforcement schedule

Review team:
- Logan Ward, Ed.M. (Behavior Specialist)
- Dr. Harris (Occupational Therapist)
- Amelia Gonzales, RN (Speech-Language Pathologist)
- Dr. Clark (Nursing)
- Parents: Jennifer Ruiz, Jacob Ruiz

**PSYCHIATRIC FOLLOW-UP:**
Emergency consultation with Dr. Allen on 4/19/2026.

Medication adjustments:
- Dosage adjustment made
- Continue current regimen with modifications

Next psychiatric appointment: 05/21/2026

**SKILL REBUILDING:**
Focus areas identified:
1. Emotion regulation and identification
2. Requesting breaks appropriately
3. Appropriate peer interactions

Teaching sessions scheduled:
- Daily emotion identification practice with Riley Richardson
- Twice weekly skills practice
- Break request training as needed throughout day

**ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATIONS:**
Changes made at 88 Geiger ICF following incident:

Physical environment:
- Designated "calm corner" with visual supports (Completed 4/19/26)
- Additional soft seating for de-escalation space

Schedule modifications:
- Individual time for preferred activities
- Structured peer activities with higher staff ratio for 1 week

**MONITORING PROTOCOL:**
Enhanced monitoring period: 10/19/2025 through 5/4/26 (2 weeks)

Monitoring frequency: Hourly emotion check-ins using 5-point scale
Documentation: Electronic incident tracking system + daily narrative notes

**CHECK-IN SCHEDULE:**
Daily check-ins with rotating staff:
- Morning: 8:30 AM (baseline mood assessment)
- Midday: 12:00 PM (activity participation check)
- Afternoon: 3:00 PM (end-of-day processing)

**PARENT COMMUNICATION PLAN:**
Daily updates to Jennifer Ruiz:
- Method: Phone call
- Time: 4:00 PM daily
- Contact: (315) 445-7890

**PROGRESS INDICATORS:**
Since incident on 4/18/2026 (48 hours post-incident):
- Zero physical aggression incidents
- Appropriate use of break request card 2 times
- Positive peer interactions during structured activities (100% appropriate)

## MODERATE CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - MULTIPLE INTERVENTIONS

**INDIVIDUALS PRESENT:**
Staff: Jackson Baker; Luke Thomas, OTR/L
Location: Community room, 100 Geiger ICF

**INCIDENT TIMELINE:**

2:10 PM - ANTECEDENT
John was participating in group activity when transition announcement was made 
to end preferred activity.

2:15 PM - BEHAVIOR ONSET
John engaged in physical aggression including:
- Pushing peer
- Throwing materials
- Verbal aggression (yelling, protesting)

2:17 PM - INITIAL INTERVENTION
Jackson Baker implemented verbal de-escalation and visual supports.
Limited effectiveness. Behavior escalated to Level 2 (moderate severity).

3:50 PM - SECONDARY INTERVENTION
Luke Thomas, OTR/L joined intervention team.
SCIP-R blocking pads utilized per BSP protocol.
John responded to planned ignoring combined with blocking strategy.

10:43 AM - DE-ESCALATION ACHIEVED
John returned to baseline. Moved to quiet room for recovery.

**INJURIES/DAMAGE:**
Staff: Jackson Baker sustained minor scratch on left forearm, no medical treatment required
Property: Game materials damaged, approximate cost $33
Client: No injuries sustained

**IMMEDIATE PARENT CONTACT:**
Jennifer Morales contacted at 315-466-3456.
Parent acknowledged incident and requested details of antecedent triggers.

Robert Morales contacted at (315) 439-9012.
Parent confirmed evening check-in call and discussed home consistency strategies.

**MEDICAL CONSULTATION:**
Nurse Sebastian Harris, MS, CCC-SLP consulted. Visual assessment of minor staff injury completed. 
No client injuries noted. No medical intervention required.

**RESTRICTIVE INTERVENTIONS USED:**
- SCIP-R Blocking Pads: Yes (Duration: 7 minutes)
- Physical Restraint: No
- Seclusion: No
- PRN Medication: Not administered

**FUNCTIONAL BEHAVIOR ASSESSMENT UPDATE:**
Data suggests escape function related to transition from preferred activities. 
Recommend FBA review with Jackson Baker scheduled for 
4/28/2026.

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Jackson was engaged in art activity at 88 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Jackson exhibited Minor non-compliance characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Henry Myers implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Jackson responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Jackson participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Jackson was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Diane Gomez at 315-434-7890. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Henry Myers
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Provider check-in:** Dr. Butler on 05/05/2026

**Client:** Rogers, Ava
**Date of Birth:** 4/10/2018
**Session Date:** 10/09/2025
**Program:** Baldwinsville TEC
**Time:** 1:00 PM - 3:00 PM
**Behavior Specialist:** Victoria Parker

---

## SKILL ACQUISITION SESSION

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Ava participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Baldwinsville TEC. Session began at 1:00 PM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 77% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 82% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 91% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 82%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**
Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
Ava demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
Ava practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Zoey Cooper, LMFT supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted William Rogers at (315) 425-8901 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Ava has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Victoria Parker
**Date signed:** 10/09/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Luke Roberts
**Incident Date:** 11/13/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 88 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** David Mendoza

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Luke was engaged in art activity at 88 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Luke exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff David Mendoza implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Luke responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
4 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Luke participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Luke was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Susan Roberts at (315)438-7890. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by David Mendoza
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/26 at 88 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Mitchell on 5/05/2026

**Report filed by:** David Mendoza
**Filed:** 11/13/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Martinez, Avery
**Incident Date:** 11/05/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 88 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Carter Nguyen

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Avery was engaged in art activity at 88 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Avery exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 5 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Carter Nguyen implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Avery responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Avery participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Avery was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Adam Martinez at (315)455-5678. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Carter Nguyen
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 88 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Ward on May 3, 2026

**Report filed by:** Carter Nguyen
**Filed:** 11/05/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

- Continue social skills group at Chadwicks TEC
- Increase peer interaction opportunities during unstructured time
- Collaborate with Dr. Fayez for social-emotional assessment

- Inviting Abigail to join activity
- Requesting turn-taking using functional communication strategies

effectively. Verbally expressed wants/needs 14 times throughout session.

**STAFF INTERACTIONS:**
Responded positively to prompts from Sebastian Rogers and Emily Wright. 
Built rapport through shared interest in activities. Accepted redirection appropriately when needed.

**GROUP ACTIVITY PARTICIPATION:**
Activity: Cooperative board game
Duration: 45 minutes
Peers present: Oliver, Abigail
Adult supervision: 1:3 staff-to-client ratio

**PARENT FEEDBACK:**
Margaret Hill attended pickup and reported Daniel has 
been initiating play with siblings at home more frequently. Contact maintained via daily communication log.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Continue social skills group at Chadwicks TEC
- Increase peer interaction opportunities during unstructured time
- Collaborate with Carter Sanders, LMHC for social-emotional assessment

**Documentation:** Sebastian Rogers, PhD, BCBA
**Date:** 10/24/2025

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** C. Jones
**Incident Date:** 10/20/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 96 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Avery Hughes

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Chloe was engaged in art activity at 96 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Chloe exhibited Minor non-compliance characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Avery Hughes implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Chloe responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Chloe participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Chloe was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Robert Jones at (315) 449-4567. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Avery Hughes
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** April 22, 2026 at 96 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Emma Taylor, LMFT on May 4, 2026

**Report filed by:** Avery Hughes
**Filed:** 10/20/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Abigail Gomez
**Incident Date:** 11/12/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 100 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Chloe Cook

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Abigail was engaged in art activity at 100 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Abigail exhibited Minor non-compliance characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 5 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Chloe Cook implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Abigail responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Abigail participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Abigail was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Patricia Gomez at (315)441-9012. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Chloe Cook
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 04/22/2026 at 100 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Bryant on April 29, 2026

**Report filed by:** Chloe Cook
**Filed:** 11/12/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**Client:** Bailey, Evelyn
**Session Date:** 11/20/2025
**Locations Observed:** 88 Geiger ICF, Syracuse TEC, Baldwinsville TEC
**Observing Staff:** Henry Martinez

---

## ENVIRONMENTAL TRIGGER DOCUMENTATION

**TRANSITION 1:** 88 Geiger ICF → Syracuse TEC
Time: 10:15 AM
Trigger: Unexpected staff change (regular driver unavailable)
Client Response: Moderate anxiety, verbal questioning, increased pacing

Evelyn demonstrated heightened anxiety when informed of transition from 
88 Geiger ICF to Syracuse TEC with unfamiliar driver. 
Environmental factors noted:
- Different vehicle than typical transport
- Substitute staff member instead of usual Henry Martinez

**TRANSITION 2:** Syracuse TEC → Baldwinsville TEC
Time: 2:15 PM
Trigger: Schedule modification due to building maintenance
Client Response: Mild agitation, requesting return to familiar setting

**SCHEDULE DISRUPTION ANALYSIS:**
Originally scheduled appointment with Olivia Reed, M.S. at Syracuse TEC on 
4/12/2026 was 
rescheduled to 5/5/2026 
due to provider illness. Evelyn exhibited increased anxiety and repetitive questioning 
about appointment status.

**PARENT CONTACT:**
Aaron Bailey contacted at 315.482.2345 to discuss 
schedule sensitivity. Parent reported Evelyn frequently references upcoming appointments 
at home and struggles with last-minute changes.

**SENSORY ENVIRONMENT ASSESSMENT:**
88 Geiger ICF: Familiar lighting, low noise level, preferred seating available
Syracuse TEC: Moderate noise level, fluorescent lighting, multiple peer interactions
Baldwinsville TEC: High activity level, variable noise, open floor plan

Consultation with Isabella Bailey, LMHC scheduled for May 20, 2026 
to assess sensory processing needs and environmental accommodation recommendations.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Increase transition warnings from 5 minutes to 15 minutes advance notice
- Environmental modifications at Syracuse TEC:
  * Provide noise-canceling headphones during high-activity periods
  * Designate quiet space for breaks
- Schedule consistency protocol - avoid changes within 48 hours when possible
- Provider coordination for appointment preparation with visual schedule

**FOLLOW-UP:**
Meeting with Aaron Bailey scheduled 
05/06/2026 
to review environmental sensitivities.

Contact Isabella Bailey, LMHC at 315-468-5678 for sensory consultation.

**Documented by:** Henry Martinez
**Date:** 11/20/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Parker, Henry
**Incident Date:** 11/12/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 92 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** David Sanders

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Henry was engaged in art activity at 92 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Henry exhibited Minor non-compliance characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 2 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff David Sanders implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Henry responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
4 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

# UCP POST-CRISIS RECOVERY SESSION NOTE

**Client:** Samuel Taylor
**Recovery Session Date:** 10/07/2025
**Original Incident Date:** April 18, 2026
**Location:** 88 Geiger ICF
**Staff:** Julian Brooks, CCC-SLP
**Clinical Supervisor:** Ava Kelly, BCBA

---

## POST-CRISIS THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION

**INCIDENT REFERENCE:**
Critical incident on April 18, 2026 at 88 Geiger ICF.
Incident Report ID: INC-2026-9455
Type: Physical aggression toward peer and staff, property destruction
Duration: Escalation 7 minutes, restraint 24 minutes

TIME SINCE INCIDENT: 48 hours

**CURRENT SESSION PURPOSE:**
1. Therapeutic processing of incident
2. Safety planning reinforcement
3. Skill rebuilding for emotion regulation
4. Relationship repair with staff and peers

**SESSION ACTIVITIES:**

**THERAPEUTIC PROCESSING:**
Samuel participated in cognitive-behavioral processing with Julian Brooks, CCC-SLP.

Discussion topics:
- Event sequence understanding using visual timeline
- Emotional identification (anger, frustration, feeling out of control)
- Alternative response strategies (asking for break, using calm-down space)
- Safety understanding (why restraint was necessary)

Samuel's insight: Demonstrated good understanding of event sequence, identified trigger, 
recognized inappropriate choice and impact on others.

**SAFETY PLANNING:**
Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Samuel.

**NEW SAFETY MEASURES IMPLEMENTED:**
Following incident on April 18, 2026:
1. Individual activity schedule - Implemented 04/19/2026
2. Enhanced visual supports for emotion regulation - Implemented April 19, 2026
3. Enhanced monitoring during peer activities (1:2 ratio)

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Joint session with James Taylor.

Parents contacted at 315.492.5678 to confirm session attendance.

Discussion points:
- Home-program consistency for emotion regulation strategies
- Warning sign recognition (escalating voice volume, body tension, pacing)
- De-escalation support at home (offering break space, reducing demands)
- Communication protocols between home and program

**STAFF RELATIONSHIP REPAIR:**
Samuel met individually with staff involved in incident.
Facilitated by: Ava Kelly, BCBA

Process included: Samuel's verbal apology, staff reassurance of continued support, 
discussion of moving forward. Staff reported positive interaction quality.

**BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT PLAN UPDATES:**
Modified BSP implemented April 19, 2026 following comprehensive review.

Changes include:
- Enhanced antecedent strategies (increased warnings before transitions)
- Additional teaching of replacement behaviors (requesting break using visual card)
- Updated crisis protocols (specific de-escalation sequence)
- Modified reinforcement schedule

Review team:
- Matthew Edwards, Direct Support Professional (Behavior Specialist)
- Dr. Scanlon (Occupational Therapist)
- Dr. Gray (Speech-Language Pathologist)
- Daniel Gonzales, Psy.D. (Nursing)
- Parents: James Taylor

**PSYCHIATRIC FOLLOW-UP:**
Emergency consultation with Dr. Hayes on 4/19/2026.

Medication adjustments:
- Added PRN protocol
- Continue current regimen with modifications

Next psychiatric appointment: 5/12/2026

**SKILL REBUILDING:**
Focus areas identified:
1. Emotion regulation and identification
2. Requesting breaks appropriately
3. Appropriate peer interactions

Teaching sessions scheduled:
- Daily emotion identification practice with Julian Brooks, CCC-SLP
- Twice weekly skills practice
- Break request training as needed throughout day

**ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATIONS:**
Changes made at 88 Geiger ICF following incident:

Physical environment:
- Designated "calm corner" with visual supports (Completed 4/19/2026)
- Additional soft seating for de-escalation space

Schedule modifications:
- Individual time for preferred activities
- Structured peer activities with higher staff ratio for 1 week

**MONITORING PROTOCOL:**
Enhanced monitoring period: 10/07/2025 through 5/4/26 (2 weeks)

Monitoring frequency: Hourly emotion check-ins using 5-point scale
Documentation: Electronic incident tracking system + daily narrative notes

**CHECK-IN SCHEDULE:**
Daily check-ins with rotating staff:
- Morning: 8:30 AM (baseline mood assessment)
- Midday: 12:00 PM (activity participation check)
- Afternoon: 3:00 PM (end-of-day processing)

**PARENT COMMUNICATION PLAN:**
Daily updates to James Taylor:
- Method: Phone call
- Time: 4:00 PM daily
- Contact: 315.492.5678

**PROGRESS INDICATORS:**
Since incident on April 18, 2026 (48 hours post-incident):
- Zero physical aggression incidents
- Appropriate use of break request card 3 times
- Positive peer interactions during structured activities (100% appropriate)
- Verbal communication of emotions using 5-point scale with 78% accuracy

**NEXT STEPS:**
☑ Continue daily monitoring through 5/4/2026
☑ BSP implementation fidelity checks (daily by supervisor)
☑ Ongoing parent collaboration (daily calls)
☑ Psychiatric follow-up 05/24/2026
☑ Incident review team meeting scheduled
☑ FBA update completion target: 4/28/2026

Recovery session documented by: Julian Brooks, CCC-SLP
Clinical supervision: Ava Kelly, BCBA
Parent consent obtained: 10/07/2025
Treatment plan updated: April 19, 2026

Session date: 10/07/2025

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Sebastian P. Alvarez
**Incident Date:** 11/04/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 92 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Charlotte Morales

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Sebastian was engaged in art activity at 92 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Sebastian exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 3 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Charlotte Morales implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Sebastian responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Sebastian participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Sebastian was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Jonathan Alvarez at (315)458-5678. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Charlotte Morales
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 92 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Hill on 04/28/2026

**Report filed by:** Charlotte Morales
**Filed:** 11/04/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** M. Gutierrez
**Incident Date:** 11/08/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 100 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Jack Moore

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Michael was engaged in art activity at 100 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Michael exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 5 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Jack Moore implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Michael responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
4 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Michael participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Michael was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Anthony Gutierrez at (315)496-4567. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Jack Moore
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 100 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Robinson on 5/4/26

**Report filed by:** Jack Moore
**Filed:** 11/08/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**ANTECEDENT:**
Sofia was engaged in art activity at 95 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Sofia exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Isabella Myers, CCC-SLP implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Sofia responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Sofia participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Sofia was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Amy Mitchell at 315-446-7890. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Isabella Myers
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 95 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Isabella Coleman, NP on 4/29/2026

**Report filed by:** Isabella Myers, CCC-SLP
**Filed:** 11/10/2025

04/17/2026 was 
rescheduled to 4/30/2026 
due to provider illness. Alexander exhibited increased anxiety and repetitive questioning 
about appointment status.

**PARENT CONTACT:**
James Robinson contacted at (315)429-8901 to discuss 
schedule sensitivity. Parent reported Alexander frequently references upcoming appointments 
at home and struggles with last-minute changes.

**SENSORY ENVIRONMENT ASSESSMENT:**
96 Geiger ICF: Familiar lighting, low noise level, preferred seating available
Cicero TEC: Moderate noise level, fluorescent lighting, multiple peer interactions
Chadwicks TEC: High activity level, variable noise, open floor plan

to assess sensory processing needs and environmental accommodation recommendations.

- Increase transition warnings from 5 minutes to 15 minutes advance notice
- Environmental modifications at Cicero TEC:

  * Designate quiet space for breaks
- Schedule consistency protocol - avoid changes within 48 hours when possible
- Provider coordination for appointment preparation with visual schedule

**FOLLOW-UP:**
Meeting with James Robinson scheduled 
5/1/26 
to review environmental sensitivities.

## MODERATE CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - MULTIPLE INTERVENTIONS

**INDIVIDUALS PRESENT:**
Staff: Jack Sanchez; Joseph Robinson, M.A.
Location: Community room, 96 Geiger ICF

**INCIDENT TIMELINE:**

10:25 AM - ANTECEDENT
Benjamin was participating in group activity when transition announcement was made 
to end preferred activity.

2:15 PM - BEHAVIOR ONSET
Benjamin engaged in physical aggression including:
- Pushing peer
- Throwing materials
- Verbal aggression (yelling, protesting)

2:17 PM - INITIAL INTERVENTION
Jack Sanchez implemented verbal de-escalation and visual supports.
Limited effectiveness. Behavior escalated to Level 2 (moderate severity).

2:20 PM - SECONDARY INTERVENTION
Joseph Robinson, M.A. joined intervention team.
SCIP-R blocking pads utilized per BSP protocol.
Benjamin responded to planned ignoring combined with blocking strategy.

3:58 PM - DE-ESCALATION ACHIEVED
Benjamin returned to baseline. Moved to quiet room for recovery.

**INJURIES/DAMAGE:**
Staff: Jack Sanchez sustained minor scratch on left forearm, no medical treatment required
Property: Game materials damaged, approximate cost $35
Client: No injuries sustained

**IMMEDIATE PARENT CONTACT:**
Brandon Ortiz contacted at 315.487.9012.
Parent acknowledged incident and requested details of antecedent triggers.

**MEDICAL CONSULTATION:**
Nurse Dr. Flores consulted. Visual assessment of minor staff injury completed.

**Observing Staff:** Lucas Sanders

---

## ENVIRONMENTAL TRIGGER DOCUMENTATION

**TRANSITION 1:** 100 Geiger ICF → Chadwicks TEC
Time: 9:30 AM
Trigger: Unexpected staff change (regular driver unavailable)
Client Response: Moderate anxiety, verbal questioning, increased pacing

Mason demonstrated heightened anxiety when informed of transition from 
100 Geiger ICF to Chadwicks TEC with unfamiliar driver. 
Environmental factors noted:
- Different vehicle than typical transport
- Substitute staff member instead of usual Lucas Sanders

**TRANSITION 2:** Chadwicks TEC → Baldwinsville TEC
Time: 2:15 PM
Trigger: Schedule modification due to building maintenance
Client Response: Mild agitation, requesting return to familiar setting

**SCHEDULE DISRUPTION ANALYSIS:**
Originally scheduled appointment with Dr. Jenkins at Chadwicks TEC on 
4/12/2026 was 
rescheduled to 5/4/26 
due to provider illness. Mason exhibited increased anxiety and repetitive questioning 
about appointment status.

**PARENT CONTACT:**
Dorothy Turner contacted at (315) 458-5678 to discuss 
schedule sensitivity. Parent reported Mason frequently references upcoming appointments 
at home and struggles with last-minute changes.

**SENSORY ENVIRONMENT ASSESSMENT:**
100 Geiger ICF: Familiar lighting, low noise level, preferred seating available
Chadwicks TEC: Moderate noise level, fluorescent lighting, multiple peer interactions
Baldwinsville TEC: High activity level, variable noise, open floor plan

Consultation with Emily Bryant, LPN scheduled for 5/18/2026 
to assess sensory processing needs and environmental accommodation recommendations.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Increase transition warnings from 5 minutes to 15 minutes advance notice
- Environmental modifications at Chadwicks TEC:
  * Provide noise-canceling headphones during high-activity periods
  * Designate quiet space for breaks
- Schedule consistency protocol - avoid changes within 48 hours when possible
- Provider coordination for appointment preparation with visual schedule

**FOLLOW-UP:**
Meeting with Dorothy Turner scheduled 
5/5/26 
to review environmental sensitivities.

Contact Emily Bryant, LPN at 315-520-5678 for sensory consultation.

**Documented by:** Lucas Sanders
**Date:** 10/13/2025

# UCP POST-CRISIS RECOVERY SESSION NOTE

**Client:** L. James
**Recovery Session Date:** 11/26/2025
**Original Incident Date:** 04/18/2026
**Location:** 95 Geiger ICF
**Staff:** Amelia Anderson
**Clinical Supervisor:** Sophia Johnson, BCBA

---

## POST-CRISIS THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION

**INCIDENT REFERENCE:**
Critical incident on 04/18/2026 at 95 Geiger ICF.
Incident Report ID: INC-2026-8994
Type: Physical aggression toward peer and staff, property destruction
Duration: Escalation 6 minutes, restraint 22 minutes

TIME SINCE INCIDENT: 48 hours

**CURRENT SESSION PURPOSE:**
1. Therapeutic processing of incident
2. Safety planning reinforcement
3. Skill rebuilding for emotion regulation
4. Relationship repair with staff and peers

**SESSION ACTIVITIES:**

**THERAPEUTIC PROCESSING:**
Lily participated in cognitive-behavioral processing with Amelia Anderson.

Discussion topics:
- Event sequence understanding using visual timeline
- Emotional identification (anger, frustration, feeling out of control)
- Alternative response strategies (asking for break, using calm-down space)
- Safety understanding (why restraint was necessary)

Lily's insight: Demonstrated good understanding of event sequence, identified trigger, 
recognized inappropriate choice and impact on others.

**SAFETY PLANNING:**
Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Lily.

**NEW SAFETY MEASURES IMPLEMENTED:**
Following incident on 04/18/2026:
1. Individual activity schedule - Implemented April 19, 2026
2. Enhanced visual supports for emotion regulation - Implemented 04/19/2026
3. Enhanced monitoring during peer activities (1:2 ratio)

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Joint session with Carol James.

Parents contacted at 315-477-5678 to confirm session attendance.

Discussion points:
- Home-program consistency for emotion regulation strategies
- Warning sign recognition (escalating voice volume, body tension, pacing)
- De-escalation support at home (offering break space, reducing demands)
- Communication protocols between home and program

**STAFF RELATIONSHIP REPAIR:**
Lily met individually with staff involved in incident.
Facilitated by: Sophia Johnson, BCBA

Process included: Lily's verbal apology, staff reassurance of continued support, 
discussion of moving forward. Staff reported positive interaction quality.

**BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT PLAN UPDATES:**
Modified BSP implemented 04/19/2026 following comprehensive review.

Changes include:
- Enhanced antecedent strategies (increased warnings before transitions)
- Additional teaching of replacement behaviors (requesting break using visual card)
- Updated crisis protocols (specific de-escalation sequence)
- Modified reinforcement schedule

Review team:
- Samuel Turner, MS, CCC-SLP (Behavior Specialist)
- Noah Rogers, RN (Occupational Therapist)
- Dr. Coleman (Speech-Language Pathologist)
- Dr. Carter (Nursing)
- Parents: Carol James

**PSYCHIATRIC FOLLOW-UP:**
Emergency consultation with Dr. Howard on 4/19/2026.

Medication adjustments:
- Increased evening anxiety medication
- Continue current regimen with modifications

Next psychiatric appointment: 5/14/2026

**SKILL REBUILDING:**
Focus areas identified:
1. Emotion regulation and identification
2. Requesting breaks appropriately
3. Appropriate peer interactions

Teaching sessions scheduled:
- Daily emotion identification practice with Amelia Anderson
- Twice weekly skills practice
- Break request training as needed throughout day

**ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATIONS:**
Changes made at 95 Geiger ICF following incident:

Physical environment:
- Designated "calm corner" with visual supports (Completed 4/19/2026)
- Additional soft seating for de-escalation space

Schedule modifications:
- Individual time for preferred activities
- Structured peer activities with higher staff ratio for 1 week

**MONITORING PROTOCOL:**
Enhanced monitoring period: 11/26/2025 through May 4, 2026 (2 weeks)

Monitoring frequency: Hourly emotion check-ins using 5-point scale
Documentation: Electronic incident tracking system + daily narrative notes

**CHECK-IN SCHEDULE:**
Daily check-ins with rotating staff:
- Morning: 8:30 AM (baseline mood assessment)
- Midday: 12:00 PM (activity participation check)
- Afternoon: 3:00 PM (end-of-day processing)

**PARENT COMMUNICATION PLAN:**
Daily updates to Carol James:
- Method: Phone call
- Time: 4:00 PM daily
- Contact: 315-477-5678

**PROGRESS INDICATORS:**
Since incident on 04/18/2026 (48 hours post-incident):
- Zero physical aggression incidents
- Appropriate use of break request card 4 times
- Positive peer interactions during structured activities (100% appropriate)
- Verbal communication of emotions using 5-point scale with 78% accuracy

**NEXT STEPS:**
☑ Continue daily monitoring through 5/4/26
☑ BSP implementation fidelity checks (daily by supervisor)
☑ Ongoing parent collaboration (daily calls)
☑ Psychiatric follow-up May 24, 2026
☑ Incident review team meeting scheduled
☑ FBA update completion target: 5/4/26

**DOCUMENTATION:**
Recovery session documented by: Amelia Anderson
Clinical supervision: Sophia Johnson, BCBA
Parent consent obtained: 11/26/2025
Treatment plan updated: 04/19/2026

Session date: 11/26/2025
Next recovery session: 04/27/2026

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Bennett, Charlotte
**Incident Date:** 11/23/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 95 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Aria Ross

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Charlotte was engaged in art activity at 95 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Charlotte exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Aria Ross implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Charlotte responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Charlotte participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Charlotte was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Richard Bennett at (315) 436-7890. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Aria Ross
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 04/22/2026 at 95 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Matthew Butler, BSN on 5/01/2026

**Report filed by:** Aria Ross
**Filed:** 11/23/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP POST-CRISIS RECOVERY SESSION NOTE

**Client:** Peterson, Wyatt
**Recovery Session Date:** 10/14/2025
**Original Incident Date:** 4/18/26
**Location:** 100 Geiger ICF
**Staff:** Jackson Bailey
**Clinical Supervisor:** Aubrey Sanders, LPN

---

## POST-CRISIS THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION

**INCIDENT REFERENCE:**
Critical incident on 4/18/26 at 100 Geiger ICF.
Incident Report ID: INC-2026-1965
Type: Physical aggression toward peer and staff, property destruction
Duration: Escalation 8 minutes, restraint 18 minutes

TIME SINCE INCIDENT: 48 hours

**CURRENT SESSION PURPOSE:**
1. Therapeutic processing of incident
2. Safety planning reinforcement
3. Skill rebuilding for emotion regulation
4. Relationship repair with staff and peers

**SESSION ACTIVITIES:**

**THERAPEUTIC PROCESSING:**
Wyatt participated in cognitive-behavioral processing with Jackson Bailey.

Discussion topics:
- Event sequence understanding using visual timeline
- Emotional identification (anger, frustration, feeling out of control)
- Alternative response strategies (asking for break, using calm-down space)
- Safety understanding (why restraint was necessary)

Wyatt's insight: Demonstrated good understanding of event sequence, identified trigger, 
recognized inappropriate choice and impact on others.

**SAFETY PLANNING:**
Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Wyatt.

**NEW SAFETY MEASURES IMPLEMENTED:**
Following incident on 4/18/26:
1. Individual activity schedule - Implemented 04/19/2026
2. Enhanced visual supports for emotion regulation - Implemented 4/19/26
3. Enhanced monitoring during peer activities (1:2 ratio)

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Joint session with Amanda Peterson.

Parents contacted at (315) 470-1234 to confirm session attendance.

Discussion points:
- Home-program consistency for emotion regulation strategies
- Warning sign recognition (escalating voice volume, body tension, pacing)
- De-escalation support at home (offering break space, reducing demands)
- Communication protocols between home and program

**STAFF RELATIONSHIP REPAIR:**
Wyatt met individually with staff involved in incident.
Facilitated by: Aubrey Sanders, LPN

Process included: Wyatt's verbal apology, staff reassurance of continued support, 
discussion of moving forward. Staff reported positive interaction quality.

**BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT PLAN UPDATES:**
Modified BSP implemented April 19, 2026 following comprehensive review.

Changes include:
- Enhanced antecedent strategies (increased warnings before transitions)
- Additional teaching of replacement behaviors (requesting break using visual card)
- Updated crisis protocols (specific de-escalation sequence)
- Modified reinforcement schedule

Review team:
- Lucas Lopez, LMFT (Behavior Specialist)
- Aria Robinson, NP (Occupational Therapist)
- Dr. Allen (Speech-Language Pathologist)
- Dr. Fayez (Nursing)
- Parents: Amanda Peterson

**PSYCHIATRIC FOLLOW-UP:**
Emergency consultation with Oliver Ross, MS, CCC-SLP on 4/19/26.

Medication adjustments:
- Added PRN protocol
- Continue current regimen with modifications

Next psychiatric appointment: 5/15/26

**SKILL REBUILDING:**
Focus areas identified:
1. Emotion regulation and identification
2. Requesting breaks appropriately
3. Appropriate peer interactions

Teaching sessions scheduled:
- Daily emotion identification practice with Jackson Bailey
- Twice weekly skills practice
- Break request training as needed throughout day

**ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATIONS:**
Changes made at 100 Geiger ICF following incident:

Physical environment:
- Designated "calm corner" with visual supports (Completed 4/19/2026)
- Additional soft seating for de-escalation space

Schedule modifications:
- Individual time for preferred activities
- Structured peer activities with higher staff ratio for 1 week

**MONITORING PROTOCOL:**
Enhanced monitoring period: 10/14/2025 through 5/4/26 (2 weeks)

Monitoring frequency: Hourly emotion check-ins using 5-point scale
Documentation: Electronic incident tracking system + daily narrative notes

**CHECK-IN SCHEDULE:**
Daily check-ins with rotating staff:
- Morning: 8:30 AM (baseline mood assessment)
- Midday: 12:00 PM (activity participation check)
- Afternoon: 3:00 PM (end-of-day processing)

**PARENT COMMUNICATION PLAN:**
Daily updates to Amanda Peterson:
- Method: Phone call
- Time: 4:00 PM daily
- Contact: (315) 470-1234

**PROGRESS INDICATORS:**
Since incident on 4/18/26 (48 hours post-incident):
- Zero physical aggression incidents
- Appropriate use of break request card 4 times
- Positive peer interactions during structured activities (100% appropriate)
- Verbal communication of emotions using 5-point scale with 76% accuracy

**NEXT STEPS:**
☑ Continue daily monitoring through May 4, 2026
☑ BSP implementation fidelity checks (daily by supervisor)
☑ Ongoing parent collaboration (daily calls)
☑ Psychiatric follow-up 5/25/26
☑ Incident review team meeting scheduled
☑ FBA update completion target: April 29, 2026

**DOCUMENTATION:**
Recovery session documented by: Jackson Bailey
Clinical supervision: Aubrey Sanders, LPN
Parent consent obtained: 10/14/2025
Treatment plan updated: 4/19/2026

Session date: 10/14/2025
Next recovery session: April 27, 2026

**Client:** M. Bailey
**Session Date:** 11/05/2025
**Locations Observed:** 92 Geiger ICF, Liverpool TEC, Baldwinsville TEC
**Observing Staff:** Logan Jones, CCC-SLP

---

## ENVIRONMENTAL TRIGGER DOCUMENTATION

**TRANSITION 1:** 92 Geiger ICF → Liverpool TEC
Time: 8:45 AM
Trigger: Unexpected staff change (regular driver unavailable)
Client Response: Moderate anxiety, verbal questioning, increased pacing

Michael demonstrated heightened anxiety when informed of transition from 
92 Geiger ICF to Liverpool TEC with unfamiliar driver. 
Environmental factors noted:
- Different vehicle than typical transport
- Substitute staff member instead of usual Logan Jones, CCC-SLP

**TRANSITION 2:** Liverpool TEC → Baldwinsville TEC
Time: 11:45 AM
Trigger: Schedule modification due to building maintenance
Client Response: Mild agitation, requesting return to familiar setting

**SCHEDULE DISRUPTION ANALYSIS:**
Originally scheduled appointment with Dr. King at Liverpool TEC on 
April 15, 2026 was 
rescheduled to 5/04/2026 
due to provider illness. Michael exhibited increased anxiety and repetitive questioning 
about appointment status.

**PARENT CONTACT:**
Diane Bailey contacted at (315) 497-3456 to discuss 
schedule sensitivity. Parent reported Michael frequently references upcoming appointments 
at home and struggles with last-minute changes.

**SENSORY ENVIRONMENT ASSESSMENT:**
92 Geiger ICF: Familiar lighting, low noise level, preferred seating available
Liverpool TEC: Moderate noise level, fluorescent lighting, multiple peer interactions
Baldwinsville TEC: High activity level, variable noise, open floor plan

Consultation with Zoey Fayez, Ph.D. scheduled for 05/19/2026 
to assess sensory processing needs and environmental accommodation recommendations.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Increase transition warnings from 5 minutes to 15 minutes advance notice
- Environmental modifications at Liverpool TEC:
  * Provide noise-canceling headphones during high-activity periods
  * Designate quiet space for breaks
- Schedule consistency protocol - avoid changes within 48 hours when possible
- Provider coordination for appointment preparation with visual schedule

**FOLLOW-UP:**
Meeting with Diane Bailey scheduled 
5/02/2026 
to review environmental sensitivities.

Contact Zoey Fayez, Ph.D. at 315-467-8901 for sensory consultation.

**Documented by:** Logan Jones, CCC-SLP
**Date:** 11/05/2025

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** R. Baker
**Incident Date:** 10/09/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 95 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Lily Carter

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Riley was engaged in art activity at 95 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Riley exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Lily Carter implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Riley responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Riley participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Riley was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Catherine Baker at 315-458-5678. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Lily Carter
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/26 at 95 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Morris on May 2, 2026

**Report filed by:** Lily Carter
**Filed:** 10/09/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - POSITIVE SOCIAL INTERACTION

**Client:** E. Gomez
**Date of Service:** 11/01/2025
**Program Location:** Cicero TEC
**Lead Therapist:** Emma Martinez
**Co-Facilitator:** Chloe Martin, BCBA

---

## POSITIVE SOCIAL ENGAGEMENT SESSION

Elizabeth demonstrated exceptional social skills during structured group activity at 
Cicero TEC from 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM.

**PEER INTERACTIONS:**
Elizabeth engaged appropriately with peers Ella and Scarlett during board game activity. 
Initiated 8 social interactions, including:
- Sharing game pieces with Ella
- Inviting Scarlett to join activity
- Requesting turn-taking using functional communication strategies

**COMMUNICATION SUCCESSES:**
Following recommendations from Dr. Torres, Elizabeth utilized total communication approach 
effectively. Verbally expressed wants/needs 11 times throughout session.

**STAFF INTERACTIONS:**
Responded positively to prompts from Emma Martinez and Chloe Martin. 
Built rapport through shared interest in activities. Accepted redirection appropriately when needed.

**GROUP ACTIVITY PARTICIPATION:**
Activity: Cooperative board game
Duration: 45 minutes
Peers present: Ella, Scarlett
Adult supervision: 1:3 staff-to-client ratio

**PARENT FEEDBACK:**
Michelle Gomez attended pickup and reported Elizabeth has 
been initiating play with siblings at home more frequently. Contact maintained via daily communication log.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Continue social skills group at Cicero TEC
- Increase peer interaction opportunities during unstructured time
- Collaborate with Dr. Torres for social-emotional assessment

**Documentation:** Emma Martinez
**Date:** 11/01/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

Jacob takes Risperidone 1mg daily per prescription from Dr. Simmons.

**FOLLOW-UP:**

Liverpool TEC from 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM.

Jackson engaged appropriately with peers John and Lily during board game activity. 
Initiated 8 social interactions, including:
- Sharing game pieces with John
- Inviting Lily to join activity
- Requesting turn-taking using functional communication strategies

**COMMUNICATION SUCCESSES:**
Following recommendations from Dr. White, Jackson utilized total communication approach 
effectively. Verbally expressed wants/needs 12 times throughout session.

**STAFF INTERACTIONS:**
Responded positively to prompts from James Hughes and Charlotte Ross. 
Built rapport through shared interest in activities. Accepted redirection appropriately when needed.

**GROUP ACTIVITY PARTICIPATION:**
Activity: Cooperative board game
Duration: 45 minutes
Peers present: John, Lily
Adult supervision: 1:3 staff-to-client ratio

**PARENT FEEDBACK:**
Steven Lopez attended pickup and reported Jackson has 
been initiating play with siblings at home more frequently. Contact maintained via daily communication log.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Continue social skills group at Liverpool TEC
- Increase peer interaction opportunities during unstructured time
- Collaborate with Dr. White for social-emotional assessment

**Documentation:** James Hughes
**Date:** 11/29/2025

---

been initiating play with siblings at home more frequently. Contact maintained via daily communication log.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Continue social skills group at Cicero TEC
- Increase peer interaction opportunities during unstructured time
- Collaborate with Dr. Cooper for social-emotional assessment

**Documentation:** Olivia Morris, M.A.
**Date:** 11/05/2025

**Date of Birth:** 12/16/2020
**Session Date:** 11/16/2025
**Program:** Cicero TEC
**Time:** 10:00 AM - 11:30 AM
**Behavior Specialist:** Aiden Young

---

## SKILL ACQUISITION SESSION

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
David participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Cicero TEC. Session began at 10:00 AM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 79% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 85% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 89% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 79%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**
Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
David demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
David practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Noah Sanchez, Ed.M. supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Linda Adams at (315) 431-8901 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported David has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Aiden Young
**Date signed:** 11/16/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

Noah was participating in group activity when transition announcement was made

Noah returned to baseline. Moved to quiet room for recovery.

Staff: Emily Morgan sustained minor scratch on left forearm, no medical treatment required

Parent confirmed evening check-in call and discussed home consistency strategies.

Nurse Dr. Jackson consulted. Visual assessment of minor staff injury completed.

- SCIP-R Blocking Pads: Yes (Duration: 9 minutes)

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Zoey participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Chadwicks TEC. Session began at 10:00 AM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 75% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 87% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 93% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 84%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**
Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
Zoey demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
Zoey practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Scarlett Morgan, LPN supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Angela Walker at 315.515.4567 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Zoey has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Avery Rogers, M.Ed.
**Date signed:** 10/28/2025

**Client:** Jackson Miller
**Date of Service:** 11/28/2025
**Program Location:** Cicero TEC
**Lead Therapist:** Grace Watson, M.A.
**Co-Facilitator:** William Hughes, Psy.D.

---

## POSITIVE SOCIAL ENGAGEMENT SESSION

Jackson demonstrated exceptional social skills during structured group activity at 
Cicero TEC from 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM.

**PEER INTERACTIONS:**
Jackson engaged appropriately with peers Liam and Sebastian during board game activity. 
Initiated 5 social interactions, including:
- Sharing game pieces with Liam
- Inviting Sebastian to join activity
- Requesting turn-taking using functional communication strategies

**COMMUNICATION SUCCESSES:**
Following recommendations from Victoria Scanlon, LMFT, Jackson utilized total communication approach 
effectively. Verbally expressed wants/needs 12 times throughout session.

**STAFF INTERACTIONS:**
Responded positively to prompts from Grace Watson and William Hughes. 
Built rapport through shared interest in activities. Accepted redirection appropriately when needed.

**GROUP ACTIVITY PARTICIPATION:**
Activity: Cooperative board game
Duration: 45 minutes
Peers present: Liam, Sebastian
Adult supervision: 1:3 staff-to-client ratio

**PARENT FEEDBACK:**
Gregory Miller attended pickup and reported Jackson has 
been initiating play with siblings at home more frequently. Contact maintained via daily communication log.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Continue social skills group at Cicero TEC
- Increase peer interaction opportunities during unstructured time
- Collaborate with Victoria Scanlon, LMFT for social-emotional assessment

**Documentation:** Grace Watson, M.A.
**Date:** 11/28/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Brooks, Wyatt
**Incident Date:** 10/10/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 92 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Sebastian Cruz

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Wyatt was engaged in art activity at 92 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Wyatt exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 3 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Sebastian Cruz implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Wyatt responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Wyatt participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Wyatt was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Justin Brooks at (315)432-5678. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Sebastian Cruz
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 04/22/2026 at 92 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Wilson on 5/04/2026

**Report filed by:** Sebastian Cruz
**Filed:** 10/10/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE
