# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** E. Gutierrez
**Incident Date:** 10/25/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 100 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Sebastian Miller

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Ethan was engaged in art activity at 100 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Ethan exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 5 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Sebastian Miller implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Ethan responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
6 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Ethan participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Ethan was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Emily Gutierrez at 315.422.3456. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Sebastian Miller
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 100 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Harris on 5/02/2026

**Report filed by:** Sebastian Miller
**Filed:** 10/25/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away

7 minutes.

Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

Ethan participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Ethan was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

Phone contact with David Ramos at (315) 483-1234.

intervention approach across settings.

- Data entered into tracking system by Elizabeth Williams

- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Ella participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Syracuse TEC. Session began at 2:00 PM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 79% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 88% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 95% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 82%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**
Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
Ella demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
Ella practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Amelia Rogers, NP supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Jeffrey Cox at (315)435-8901 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Ella has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** David Martin
**Date signed:** 10/03/2025

---

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Jack B. Ward
**Incident Date:** 11/01/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 96 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Charlotte Mitchell

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Jack was engaged in art activity at 96 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Jack exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Charlotte Mitchell implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Jack responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Jack participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Jack was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Rachel Ward at 315.460.4567. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Charlotte Mitchell
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 96 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Perez on May 4, 2026

**Report filed by:** Charlotte Mitchell
**Filed:** 11/01/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**Behavior Specialist:** Matthew Harris, M.Ed.

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Wyatt participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Baldwinsville TEC. Session began at 9:00 AM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 76% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 85% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 94% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 86%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**
Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
Wyatt demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
Wyatt practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Sofia Price, LMFT supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Brandon Roberts at (315)443-9012 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Wyatt has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Matthew Harris, M.Ed.
**Date signed:** 11/12/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**Program Location:** Syracuse TEC

**Co-Facilitator:** Victoria Morales, Behavior Specialist II

---

## POSITIVE SOCIAL ENGAGEMENT SESSION

Alexander demonstrated exceptional social skills during structured group activity at 
Syracuse TEC from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM.

**PEER INTERACTIONS:**
Alexander engaged appropriately with peers Evelyn and Julian during board game activity. 
Initiated 7 social interactions, including:
- Sharing game pieces with Evelyn
- Inviting Julian to join activity
- Requesting turn-taking using functional communication strategies

**COMMUNICATION SUCCESSES:**
Following recommendations from Dr. Hill, Alexander utilized total communication approach 
effectively. Verbally expressed wants/needs 12 times throughout session.

**STAFF INTERACTIONS:**
Responded positively to prompts from Lucas Howard and Victoria Morales. 
Built rapport through shared interest in activities. Accepted redirection appropriately when needed.

**GROUP ACTIVITY PARTICIPATION:**
Activity: Cooperative board game
Duration: 45 minutes
Peers present: Evelyn, Julian
Adult supervision: 1:3 staff-to-client ratio

**PARENT FEEDBACK:**
Rebecca Mendoza attended pickup and reported Alexander has 
been initiating play with siblings at home more frequently. Contact maintained via daily communication log.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Continue social skills group at Syracuse TEC
- Increase peer interaction opportunities during unstructured time
- Collaborate with Dr. Hill for social-emotional assessment

**Documentation:** Lucas Howard
**Date:** 11/29/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Carter, Jackson
**Incident Date:** 10/25/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 88 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Olivia Jones

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Jackson was engaged in art activity at 88 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Jackson exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Olivia Jones implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Jackson responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
6 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Jackson participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Jackson was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Jonathan Carter at (315)500-1234. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Olivia Jones
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 88 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Russell on 4/28/26

**Report filed by:** Olivia Jones
**Filed:** 10/25/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**Client:** Levi Thomas
**Date of Birth:** 2/15/2016
**Session Date:** 11/24/2025
**Program:** Baldwinsville TEC
**Time:** 9:00 AM - 10:00 AM
**Behavior Specialist:** Lucas Kim

---

## SKILL ACQUISITION SESSION

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Levi participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Baldwinsville TEC. Session began at 9:00 AM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 73% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 85% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 88% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 81%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**
Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
Levi demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
Levi practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Michael Wood, Behavior Specialist I supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Jessica Thomas at 315.501.7890 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Levi has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Lucas Kim
**Date signed:** 11/24/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

- Collaborate with Dr. Adams for social-emotional assessment

**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

Joseph participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Cicero TEC. Session began at 1:00 PM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

Parent reported Joseph has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Amelia Wood
**Date signed:** 11/12/2025

---

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Nguyen, Daniel
**Incident Date:** 10/17/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 95 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Zoey Wright, CCC-SLP

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Daniel was engaged in art activity at 95 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Daniel exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 5 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Zoey Wright, CCC-SLP implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Daniel responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
6 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Daniel participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Daniel was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Kimberly Nguyen at (315)449-4567. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Zoey Wright
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 95 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Matthew Bailey, Behavior Specialist I on April 28, 2026

**Report filed by:** Zoey Wright, CCC-SLP
**Filed:** 10/17/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Abigail participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Chadwicks TEC. Session began at 10:00 AM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

- Trial block 2: 85% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 91% accuracy across 15 trials

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
Abigail practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Aria Ortiz, LMHC supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Jeffrey Allen at (315)423-8901 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Abigail has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Victoria Hall
**Date signed:** 11/29/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

effectively. Verbally expressed wants/needs 13 times throughout session.

Responded positively to prompts from Ava Robinson and Aiden Robinson. 
Built rapport through shared interest in activities. Accepted redirection appropriately when needed.

Activity: Cooperative board game

Deborah Lewis attended pickup and reported Elizabeth has 
been initiating play with siblings at home more frequently. Contact maintained via daily communication log.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Continue social skills group at Baldwinsville TEC
- Increase peer interaction opportunities during unstructured time
- Collaborate with Dr. James for social-emotional assessment

**Documentation:** Ava Robinson
**Date:** 10/21/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - SKILL ACQUISITION

**Client:** Lily Myers
**Date of Birth:** 10/17/15
**Session Date:** 10/06/2025
**Program:** Chadwicks TEC
**Time:** 9:00 AM - 11:00 AM
**Behavior Specialist:** Elijah Morales

---

## SKILL ACQUISITION SESSION

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Lily participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Chadwicks TEC. Session began at 9:00 AM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 77% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 89% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 92% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 84%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**
Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
Lily demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
Lily practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Amelia Garcia, Behavior Specialist supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Patricia Myers at 315-459-4567 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Lily has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Elijah Morales
**Date signed:** 10/06/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

Abigail was engaged in art activity at 96 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Abigail exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 2 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Ava Ramos, PhD, BCBA implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Abigail responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
4 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Abigail participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Abigail was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Anthony Gomez at 315.448.8901. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Ava Ramos
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 96 Geiger ICF

# UCP SESSION NOTE - SKILL ACQUISITION

**Client:** Luke Ramirez
**Date of Birth:** 11/27/2020
**Session Date:** 10/21/2025
**Program:** Cicero TEC
**Time:** 3:00 PM - 5:00 PM
**Behavior Specialist:** Amelia Johnson

---

## SKILL ACQUISITION SESSION

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Luke participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Cicero TEC. Session began at 3:00 PM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 71% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 85% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 89% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 79%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**
Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
Luke demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
Luke practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Carter Peterson, Ph.D. supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Helen Ramirez at (315)425-8901 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Luke has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Amelia Johnson
**Date signed:** 10/21/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

- Reduce prompting to gestural level only

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Aria participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Baldwinsville TEC. Session began at 1:00 PM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 74% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 86% accuracy across 15 trials

Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end.

Aria practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Aiden Bennett, BSN supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Catherine Chavez at 315.451.3456 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Aria has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Lucas Carter
**Date signed:** 10/30/2025

observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

Jacob was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**Client:** Taylor, Oliver
**Incident Date:** 11/03/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 92 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Benjamin Edwards

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Oliver was engaged in art activity at 92 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Oliver exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 3 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Benjamin Edwards implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Oliver responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
4 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Oliver participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Oliver was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Laura Taylor at 315.440.7890. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Benjamin Edwards
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 92 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Collins on 4/30/2026

**Report filed by:** Benjamin Edwards
**Filed:** 11/03/2025

---

Responded positively to prompts from Riley Edwards and Ethan Ortiz. 
Built rapport through shared interest in activities. Accepted redirection appropriately when needed.

Activity: Cooperative board game

Peers present: Zoey, Olivia
Adult supervision: 1:3 staff-to-client ratio

**PARENT FEEDBACK:**
Nancy Cox attended pickup and reported Liam has 
been initiating play with siblings at home more frequently. Contact maintained via daily communication log.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Continue social skills group at Cicero TEC
- Increase peer interaction opportunities during unstructured time
- Collaborate with Isabella Robinson, Psy.D. for social-emotional assessment

**Documentation:** Riley Edwards
**Date:** 11/27/2025

# UCP SESSION NOTE - ENVIRONMENTAL TRIGGER ANALYSIS

**Client:** Elijah Phillips
**Session Date:** 10/23/2025
**Locations Observed:** 92 Geiger ICF, Liverpool TEC, Chadwicks TEC
**Observing Staff:** Owen Walker

---

## ENVIRONMENTAL TRIGGER DOCUMENTATION

**TRANSITION 1:** 92 Geiger ICF → Liverpool TEC
Time: 10:15 AM
Trigger: Unexpected staff change (regular driver unavailable)
Client Response: Moderate anxiety, verbal questioning, increased pacing

Elijah demonstrated heightened anxiety when informed of transition from 
92 Geiger ICF to Liverpool TEC with unfamiliar driver. 
Environmental factors noted:
- Different vehicle than typical transport
- Substitute staff member instead of usual Owen Walker

**TRANSITION 2:** Liverpool TEC → Chadwicks TEC
Time: 2:15 PM
Trigger: Schedule modification due to building maintenance
Client Response: Mild agitation, requesting return to familiar setting

**SCHEDULE DISRUPTION ANALYSIS:**
Originally scheduled appointment with Ava Clark, Ed.M. at Liverpool TEC on 
4/14/2026 was 
rescheduled to 4/29/2026 
due to provider illness. Elijah exhibited increased anxiety and repetitive questioning 
about appointment status.

**PARENT CONTACT:**
Tyler Phillips contacted at (315) 503-9012 to discuss 
schedule sensitivity. Parent reported Elijah frequently references upcoming appointments 
at home and struggles with last-minute changes.

**SENSORY ENVIRONMENT ASSESSMENT:**
92 Geiger ICF: Familiar lighting, low noise level, preferred seating available
Liverpool TEC: Moderate noise level, fluorescent lighting, multiple peer interactions
Chadwicks TEC: High activity level, variable noise, open floor plan

Consultation with Dr. Flores scheduled for 5/17/2026 
to assess sensory processing needs and environmental accommodation recommendations.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Increase transition warnings from 5 minutes to 15 minutes advance notice
- Environmental modifications at Liverpool TEC:
  * Provide noise-canceling headphones during high-activity periods
  * Designate quiet space for breaks
- Schedule consistency protocol - avoid changes within 48 hours when possible
- Provider coordination for appointment preparation with visual schedule

**FOLLOW-UP:**
Meeting with Tyler Phillips scheduled 
5/4/2026 
to review environmental sensitivities.

Contact Dr. Flores at 315-465-9012 for sensory consultation.

**Documented by:** Owen Walker
**Date:** 10/23/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**Client:** A. Thompson
**Date of Birth:** 6/27/19
**Session Date:** 11/01/2025
**Program:** Liverpool TEC
**Time:** 1:00 PM - 2:00 PM
**Behavior Specialist:** Harper Jones, M.Ed.

---

## SKILL ACQUISITION SESSION

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Aubrey participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Liverpool TEC. Session began at 1:00 PM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 71% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 88% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 93% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 85%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**
Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
Aubrey demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
Aubrey practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Chloe Phillips, LCSW supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Charles Thompson at 315-484-2345 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Aubrey has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Harper Jones, M.Ed.
**Date signed:** 11/01/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Amelia L. Cruz
**Incident Date:** 10/17/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 96 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Charlotte Thompson

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Amelia was engaged in art activity at 96 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Amelia exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 3 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Charlotte Thompson implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Amelia responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Amelia participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Amelia was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Catherine Cruz at (315)446-7890. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Charlotte Thompson
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** April 22, 2026 at 96 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Turner on 5/5/2026

**Report filed by:** Charlotte Thompson
**Filed:** 10/17/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

## SKILL ACQUISITION SESSION

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Samuel participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Syracuse TEC. Session began at 3:00 PM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 71% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 83% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 93% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 83%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**
Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
Samuel demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
Samuel practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Julian Anderson, Sr. BCBA supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Justin Robinson at (315)504-5678 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Samuel has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Avery Cox
**Incident Date:** 10/29/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 95 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Carter Parker

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Avery was engaged in art activity at 95 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Avery exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 3 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Carter Parker implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Avery responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
4 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Avery participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Avery was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Tyler Cox at 315-491-1234. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Carter Parker
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** April 22, 2026 at 95 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Turner on 5/01/2026

**Report filed by:** Carter Parker
**Filed:** 10/29/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Morgan, Jack
**Incident Date:** 10/12/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 88 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Daniel Mitchell, CCC-SLP

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Jack was engaged in art activity at 88 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Jack exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Daniel Mitchell, CCC-SLP implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Jack responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Jack participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Jack was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Steven Morgan at (315)461-5678. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Daniel Mitchell
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 88 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Collins on 05/02/2026

**Report filed by:** Daniel Mitchell, CCC-SLP
**Filed:** 10/12/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Jack Nelson
**Incident Date:** 11/22/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 92 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Julian Price

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Jack was engaged in art activity at 92 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Jack exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Julian Price implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Jack responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Jack participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Jack was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Catherine Nelson at (315)429-8901. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Julian Price
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/26 at 92 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Griffin on 5/3/26

**Report filed by:** Julian Price
**Filed:** 11/22/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE
